title: ‘The Drop’ Trailer Sees ‘Snowfall’ Characters Go After “New Gold Rush” of West Coast Rap
full_text: × Skip to main content By Hilary Lewis Plus Icon Hilary Lewis Deputy Editor, East Coast hilarylewis Follow Sign Up View All August 17, 2026 5:14pm Isaiah John (left), Asante Blackk, Gail Bean and Peyton Alex Smith in 'The Drop: A Snowfall Saga.' FX After getting clean, Gail Bean’s Snowfall character Wanda Bell has her sights set on the music business. In the trailer for Snowfall spinoff, The Drop , set to premiere on Tuesday Sept. 8 on FX and Hulu , Wanda is shown proclaiming that West Coast rap “is the new gold rush; no cops, no murder” She then goes to her cousin Lamar (Asante Blackk) and asks him to make a beat for her as the two of them try to attract volatile local rapper Artillery (Simmie “Buddy” Sims III). Related Stories TV 'Deli Boys' Canceled After Two Seasons on Hulu TV 'American Horror Story: 13' First Teaser Returns Jessica Lange, Evan Peters, Twisty the Clown, Rubber Man and More for All-Star Season And, via voiceover, as the tapes start piling up, she explains how what she witnessed with Leon and Franklin ( Snowfall star Damson Idris) building their crack empire, gave her a “front-row seat to how they changed the game. We know our customers because they are our customers.” As the trailer goes on, the tensions on the streets ratchet up as family members disapprove of Lamar getting involved with the rap game and Wanda’s threatened more than once. And Leon suggests Wanda may be in over her head. “I know these streets just like you,” she tells him. “But you don’t know this gangsta business like me,” he replies. Still she ends the preview on a high: “I’m unstoppable, baby!” Here’s the synopsis for the new series, set in ’90s Los Angeles, which Snowfall jumped ahead to in its 2023 series finale , with Leon telling Franklin that Wanda was trying to make it in music. “ The Drop: A Snowfall Saga follows Snowfall characters Wanda Bell (Gail Bean) and Leon Simmons (Isaiah John) as they fight to reinvent themselves in ’90s Los Angeles, where the fallout from the crack epidemic is fueling a new game: the rise of West Coast rap. Wanda starts the series driven by the clear belief that West Coast rap has the power to reshape American culture. She will work to put together a ragtag group of geniuses and lead them to the realization of all their dreams. To do it, she must navigate the dangerous overlap of music and street politics, pulling in those closest to her including her cousins Lamar Kinsey (Asante Blackk) and James Kinsey (Peyton Alex Smith), and pursuing volatile local rapper Artillery (Simmie “Buddy” Sims III), who is already in a tangle with law enforcement. Her internship with former D-boy-turned-label-owner Darryl ‘DG’ Grant (Brandon Mychal Smith) creates opportunities but also deepens tensions between Wanda and Leon, who has vowed to leave the streets for good and chase down his own atonement through his free legal clinic. As ambition, loyalty and survival collide, how much is everyone willing to risk in order to build something lasting in a world that threatens to pull them down?” The cast also includes Mykelti Williamson, Nicki Micheaux, Isidora Goreshter, Eric Balfour, Richard Portnow, Zaire Adams, Demetrius Grosse and Quincy Chad, with Chad reprising his Snowfall role as Big Leon. Malcolm Spellman ( The Falcon and the Winter Soldier, Bel-Air ) executive produces the series from FX Productions with Snowfall EPs Dave Andron, Thomas Schlamme, Julie DeJoie, Michael London, Trevor Engelson and Paul Garnes. Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter for the Snowfall finale, Andron explained crafting the narrative so Leon and Wanda, then happily married, could move forward. “One of our guiding lights for who was going to make it out was: The people who had taken stock of the things they’d done and tried to change their lives should get to make it out,” he said, naming Leon as one of those characters. “It felt like you wanted there to be, for those people, a chance to go live a life. They get a chance to go forward and try to right the wrongs of their past. That felt important as well. Because the reality is it’s not just hopeless for everybody. But that was the guiding light for who gets a happier ending.” THR

title: Before She Hosts Primetime Emmy Awards, Mariska Hargitay Goes For Gold With Triple Nominee ‘My Mom Jayne’
full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Lightdox Acquires ‘Auber 89’ Ahead Of Doc’s World Premiere at Venice Film Festival Sidebar Giornate Degli Autori ‘Traces Of Home’ Trailer: Award-Winning Film From EPs Melissa Barrera And John Leguizamo Tells Story Of Love And Forced Displacement ‘First They Came For My College,’ Film About Ron DeSantis-Led “Hostile Takeover” Of Florida School, Announces Theatrical Run View All August 17, 2026 5:05pm Mariska Hargitay in 'My Mom Jayne' HBO As Mariska Hargitay reflects on the past year in her life – a momentous one for the actress and filmmaker – a word comes to her mind to describe it: “cathartic.” She completed her 27 th season starring as Capt. Olivia Benson on Law & Order: SVU and in May made her Broadway debut in the drama Every Brilliant Thing – both exceptional achievements. But the catharsis emerged through an even more personal endeavor: her nonfiction directorial debut My Mom Jayne . The HBO documentary, an intimate exploration of Hargitay’s mother, the late actress Jayne Mansfield , and of a mystery surrounding the identity of Hargitay’s father, has earned three Primetime Emmy nominations, including Outstanding Documentary or Nonfiction Special and Outstanding Directing for a Nonfiction Program. Related Stories News Everything We Know About 'The Gilded Age' Season 4 So Far News Showtime! Buss Family Sells Remaining Lakers Stake To Bob Iger & Josh Kushner “The film has been, for me, the gift that just keeps on giving,” she tells Deadline. “It was an archeological dig of me not knowing what I was going to find, hoping that I had the internal architecture to support myself… Going into the unknown and not knowing what the other side was going to look like, it’s been so extraordinary to come out the other side with the results beyond my even dreams or comprehension, not knowing that the film would resonate with so many people the way it has.” Watch on Deadline Hargitay was just three years old when her mother was tragically killed in an auto accident outside New Orleans in 1967. Mariska and her two older brothers, Zoltán and Miklos (Mickey Jr.), were in the back seat of the vehicle but survived. Mariska and her older siblings were raised by Mickey Hargitay Sr., the man she grew up believing to be her biological father. Jayne Mansfield in 1957. Everett Collection Jayne Mansfield possessed great beauty and talent. She was multilingual and played classical piano and violin, but her exceptional good looks and curvaceous figure limited how the men who ran Hollywood perceived her. Mansfield accommodated herself to the sex symbol persona. In the film, Hargitay recalls growing up without her mom and becoming uncomfortable with how Mansfield had presented on screen. “I didn’t really appreciate the sort of bombshell image and didn’t like some of the [acting] choices she made,” Hargitay told us at the Cannes Film Festival, where My Mom Jayne premiered. “I felt myself being embarrassed by her and just wanting a normal mom and a regular mom and ‘pick me up from school’ and like that… I just felt like I dissociated myself and said, yeah, I don’t want to be part of that, and I want to do it differently.” Executive producer Lauran Bromley, director Mariska Hargitay, and producer and Trish Adlesic pose during the ‘My Mom Jayne: A Film By Mariska Hargitay’ photocall at the 78th annual Cannes Film Festival on May 18, 2025. Pascal Le Segretain/Getty Images In the course of the film, Hargitay reevaluates her mom, forming a fuller picture of how Mansfield’s career choices were circumscribed by the egregious sexism of the 1950s and ‘60s. She also explores her mother’s complicated love life, and the blended family Jayne raised that included Mickey Hargitay’s daughter by his first wife. The honesty of the portrayal, coupled with the reality that many people experience blended families or complicated family dynamics has allowed viewers to connect with the film. A young Mariska Hargitay with her mom, Jayne Mansfield. HBO Documentary Films “You could say, ‘Oh, [this story is] about Jayne Mansfield, a movie star in the ’50s and her TV star daughter’; that’s not what the movie is about. It’s a family film. It’s a story about generational trauma, and it’s a story about identity and recovery and reclamation and forgiveness and so many things,” Hargitay says, expressing pride in “the way the film has been received and the way that people have said, ‘That’s my story,’ and the spark that has led people to investigate their own families to uncover their family secrets or just deal with them or just look at them closer.” Hargitay captures on screen her reaction to learning as an adult that Mickey Hargitay in fact wasn’t her biological father. Her dad was Nelson Sardelli, a Brazilian singer with whom Jayne Mansfield became romantically involved during a break from her marriage to Hargitay. That revelation triggered conflicting emotions in Mariska, who felt intensely loyal to Mickey Hargitay as her loving father and didn’t want it to seem as if, somehow, she were turning her back on him. “When we keep secrets, I think that occupies a big part of our psyche — knowingly and unconsciously,” Hargitay observes. “Holding this secret and feeling bad about it and knowing that there was a part of me that just wasn’t clear and allowing myself to be my authentic self — but out of duty thinking this is how it had to be to honor my father. And then when I came to the realization like, no, no, no, that secret isn’t honoring anyone. We have to tell the secret.” She adds, “I wanted to make a love letter for my father, Mickey. That’s what I wanted to do. But in the process, it turned out to really be a love letter to all three of them [Jayne, Nelson, and Mickey] because the film deals with the complexity of the human condition, the real complexities of what it is to be human and how two things can be true at once… I wanted to understand why. Who was the woman behind the pose? Why did my father never admit to me? Why did Nelson never claim me? And I got answers to all of it, and the answers were the most loving.” In My Mom Jayne , Mariska connects with Nelson Sardelli, and the half-sisters she never knew she had. “It was very cathartic and mind-blowing to hear Nelson’s side of the story and understanding why he made the decisions that he made and how complex the decisions were for all three of them in so many ways,” she shares. “I was freed up; I felt like this giant exhale.” Mariska Hargitay acknowledges the audience after making her Broadway debut in ‘Every Brilliant Thing’ at the Hudson Theatre on June 2, 2026. Rob Kim/Getty Images The freeing of psychic space has allowed Hargitay to pursue new avenues of creativity. She made her Broadway debut 40 years after her late mother had done the same. “She was 22 [when she made her debut] and I was 62. That was also a deeply extraordinary feeling for me,” Hargitay affirms. “And when I went to Broadway, one of the things that I took with me was a plaque that she got that said ‘Broadway’s Rising Star 1955.’ And so every night I would hold that before I went [on stage].” Hargitay will continue an extraordinary year by embarking on the 28 th season of Law & Order: SVU and taking on another major challenge – hosting the Primetime Emmy Awards on NBC on Monday, Sept. 14. We’ll have more on Mariska’s plans for hosting the show in a separate piece we’ll publish on Tuesday. She won’t be simultaneously hosting and hearing announcements of winners in the documentary categories – those are presented at the Creative Arts Emmys ceremony in Los Angeles on Sept. 5 and 6. ‘Nashville’ & ‘Heroes’ Star Dies At 36; Career In Photos; Tributes Spidey Posts 2nd-Best Third Frame Ever; ‘Oak Street’ Out-Dinos ‘PAW Patrol’ Demands Huge Bond From AGs & WGA Over Costs Of “Roadblock” Suit HBO Renews ‘IT: Welcome To Derry’ For Season 2; Brad Caleb Kane Sole Showrunner Read More About: 1 Comments

title: Round Hill Files $1 Billion Copyright Infringement Suits Against Suno, Anthropic
full_text: Skip to main content By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All August 17, 2026 4:46pm Getty Images Logo text Independent music publisher Round Hill is suing Suno and Anthropic on claims of mass copyright infringement, alleging that the two AI companies scraped hundreds of the publisher’s songs without permission to train their AI models. Round Hill marks just the latest major lawsuit for both Suno and Anthropic, who’ve both been sued by the major record companies on similar claims. Suno, industry’s biggest AI music generation platform, also faces a suit from Universal Music Group and Sony Music Group (WMG also sued, though the company has since settled ) related to its use of copyright to create new AI-generated recordings. Anthropic, meanwhile faces suits from Universal Music Publishing, Abcko, Concord and BMG over the companies’ songs’ lyrics being used to train its AI agent Claude. Round Hill is a prominent music publisher whose copyrights include the Goo Goo Dolls’ “Iris,” Bonnie Tyler’s “Total Eclipse of the Heart,” the Kinks’ “Lola” and Dio’s “Holy Diver.” The company provided a list of 500 songs that the defendants had infringed upon. Round Hill said in the suits that the company plans to “amend to list potentially ten thousand or more of their musical compositions,” with those damages potentially exceeding $1 billion. “While in other cases for copyright infringement, Defendant has waxed poetic about the necessity of progress and AI’s value to society, there is simply no reason — other than rote expediency — to have that progress come at the cost of copyrights holders,” prominent music attorney Richard Busch, representing Round Hill, wrote in the suits. Round Hill further argued that the latter “‘expediency’ arguments completely falter” when taking into account Suno and Anthropic’s significant cash valuations they’ve earned while “exploiting illicit copies of copyrighted works, including the Round Hill Works.” “There is simply nothing fair about a company using theft to build for purely commercial purposes a multi-billion dollar business while those from which they steal receive nothing,” Round Hill said. Reps for Anthropic and Suno didn’t immediately respond to request for comment. THR

title: Inside Netflix’s Field of Dreams Face-Off in Iowa: “A Magical Moment”
full_text: × Skip to main content Minnesota Twins and Philadelphia Phillies players (with coach Don Mattingly) walk out of the corn field before the start of the Field of Dreams game between the Philadelphia Phillies and the Minnesota Twins in Dyersville, Iowa, on Aug. 13, 2026. Patrick McDermott/Netflix They built it, and thousands came. The Field of Dreams movie site in Dyersville, Iowa, roared back to life last Thursday to host upwards of 8,000 fans, 26 Hall of Famers and VIPs like Theo Von to take in Major League Baseball ‘s regular season matchup between the Philadelphia Phillies and Minnesota Twins. The high-profile outing, presented by John Deere and streamed live on Netflix , marked only the third MLB game to be played on the grounds where director Phil Alden Robinson filmed the beloved 1989 sports drama starring Kevin Costner. Related Stories General News Theo Von Takes Break From Field of Dreams Game to Talk Road Trips, Staying Healthy And Loving Iowa Movies Patrick Renna on 'The Sandlot' Fame and "Once in a Lifetime" Trip to Field of Dreams Game in Iowa But it was the first in four years and the first to take place inside a newly constructed, permanent stadium adjacent to the movie’s original baseball field and farmhouse. True to its inspiration, it’s also framed by meticulously arranged cornrows, which guests passed through in order to access the stadium. The wait (and the walk) amped up the anticipation, and one could feel the excitement on the grounds as gates opened for press and special guests hours ahead of the 6:30 p.m. start time. It also helped that rain clouds that had been dumping on Iowa all week dried up just in the nick of time. The movie site filled up first as fans flocked to take photographs of the scene and mingle with “ghost” players who were keen to play catch (with gloves and balls available to use free of charge). Star players from the Phillies and Twins also roamed the field freely with families, friends and fellow players. It was a uniquely special sight that even saw Phillies managing partner and chief executive officer John Middleton hitting the infield to play catch with his grandsons. It was a pinch-me day for Phillies player and Iowa native Derek Hill, who hails from Des Moines. “It means a lot to me to be here, but I think it means more to the state by bringing the recognition,” he told The Hollywood Reporter . “Seeing all these people out here enjoying the game of baseball and tying it back to the movie, it’s incredible.” Hill has seen the film “countless times” over the course of his 30 years, joking that he “probably watched it the day I was born with my pops.” The film is currently on Netflix, and the streamer must have seen a bit of a surge in viewership, as nearly every person THR encountered at the field said they watched it again in recent days or weeks leading up to the game. “I watched it on an airplane the other day because I knew we were coming here,” Von told THR from his seat mid-game. “I wanted to relight the candle a little bit. It’s a nice story about a father-son that really brings people together. I’ve run into some fathers and sons here at the ballpark today, so that’s been really cool and kind of heartwarming to see.” Hollywood has had a rough go in recent years, so it’s heartwarming for many industry insiders to hear just how alive the legacy is for one of its exports, especially after the passing of decades. Though he wasn’t in attendance, producer Larry Gordon just recently shared what an uphill battle it was to get the picture made back in the ’80s. “Whenever you think you have a hard pitch to sell, think about this one: A farmer plows on his corn crop to build a baseball diamond so that the ghost of Shoeless Joe Jackson comes back to the team of dead players all because one day working in his field that farmer heard an unattached voice whisper to him in a very easy to decipher message that anyone would quickly get: ‘If you build it, he would come,'” Gordon said while accepting Producers United’s Legacy Award on Sherry Lansing’s back lawn. “We were turned down and practically thrown out by every studio more than once. It took years, but we got it made.” The film went on to secure three Academy Award nominations, including one for best picture. Robinson also snagged one for best adapted screenplay, which was based on Canadian novelist W. P. Kinsella’s 1982 novel Shoeless Joe. Iconic lines and script passages — “is this heaven?” to “if you build it, he will come” — were peppered throughout the grounds, from Fanatics merch stands and backdrops to billboards. Hall of Famer CC Sabathia, who parted the cornrows to walk on the field as part of a group of 26 legends before the first pitch, told THR that he only watched the film for the first time last week. “I loved it,” said Sabathia, who also joined Netflix as an on-screen commentator for the broadcast. “When you watch the movie, it gets you back into the memories of what got you into baseball in the first place. Baseball is one of those sports that relies on an older father, brother, grandfather or uncle to play catch with you, toss some ground balls, pitches or pop-ups. For me, I was an only child and there were three people — my dad and two uncles — who were never too tired to play with me. They meant a lot to me so watching the movie meant a lot to me because of them.” Netflix and the MLB pulled out all the stops and a gaggle of talent to fill out the broadcast. On the scene were broadcasters Anthony Rizzo, Elle Duncan, Matt Vasgersian and Lauren Shehadi along with baseball greats Sabathia, Barry Bonds and Albert Pujols who joined the telecast to provide insider commentary. “I’m glad that Netflix jumped into bed with us to be able to bring the sport to a wider fan base,” Sabathia told THR of the streamer’s recent and inaugural foray into MLB action with three events : opening night in March, the Home Run Derby in July and the Field of Dreams game . “Netflix has hit it right on the money with trying to expand the fan base.” The push is part of a wider trend in sports to eventize regular season games to rally existing fans while embracing new ones. “The challenge for baseball is how do you create these jewel events in a schedule that requires 162 games be played in a 180-day window? It’s very difficult,” Vasgersian said. “As opposed to doing a game from an iconic ballpark that’s been around for a hundred years, like Fenway Park in Boston or Wrigley Field in Chicago, where you’re just steeped in the history, the history for the Field of Dreams game is really accessible. The film is not that old in the grand scheme of things, and the movie set still exists. It’s not like going to Universal Studios and seeing the New York street sets and having somebody tell you, ‘This is where they shot the movie.’ This is here and it’s special.” Shehadi agreed. “I always talk about moments in time in life. This is a moment in time for me. It’s one of those things that I’ll think about for the rest of my life. I grew up around this game. I was at the ball field when I was seven years old and my dad and mom would drop me off. And I grew this deep love, this deep love for the game,” she explained. “This game is for love of sport and love of country. Having this game in such a beautiful place at the Field of Dreams, it takes you back to your childhood to those simple, pure times. … That’s what this game represents. It’s a magical moment in time.” If you ask anyone in attendance at the game, they would also cite the magical moment of watching those 26 Hall of Famers emerge from the cornfield in the outfield to make their way to the infield to be introduced by Schwarber and fellow All-Star Byron Buxton of the Twins. Newly inducted Hall of Famers Andruw Jones and Jeff Kent had the honor of throwing out the first pitches while Alana Springsteen sang the National Anthem. Schwarber did his best to keep the good vibes going. As the first batter to kick off the game, he smashed a home run deep into right field for what would be his first of two. It was greeted by fireworks. “It’s so cool to see a ball disappear into a cornfield,” said a fan seated near THR . In total, there were four home runs (three for Philadelphia and one for Minnesota) as the Phillies rallied to beat the Twins 7-1. Aside from the fully grown stalks in the fields, corn was seemingly everywhere. There was a corn shucking contest, elote corn bites at concession stands and fans decked out in corn costumes or hats. Before the game and in between innings, fans kept busy playing cornhole. After the final pitch had been thrown, Phillies players ran onto the field to celebrate their victory. The final score and the entire experience delivered a Hollywood ending for Iowa native Hill, who was seen taking an ear of corn as a souvenir. He said, “It was really cool to be able to come back here and live out my dream.” Hill snags a souvenir after his team won the MLB matchup. title: Kevin Macdonald On Capturing Pep Guardiola For Prime Video’s ‘A Beautiful Obsession’: “Like Having Robert De Niro Play A Football Coach”
full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Kevin Macdonald On Capturing Pep Guardiola For Prime Video’s ‘A Beautiful Obsession’: “Like Having Robert De Niro Play A Football Coach” ‘Small Town Scandal’: ‘Only Murders In The Building’-Inspired Show From New Zealand Comic Royalty Proves Podcasts Can Be Perfect “Proof Of Concept” ‘The Boys’ VFX Firm Untold Hires Film & Episodic Chief View All August 17, 2026 4:01pm Pep Guardiola City Studios “Pep playing himself is a bit like having Robert De Niro play a football coach.” Those are the musings of Oscar-winning director Kevin Macdonald , who has just spent two years charting the exploits of Pep Guardiola and Manchester City for A Beautiful Obsession and yet had barely heard of Guardiola before he was brought on board by Prime Video, Plan B , Workerbee and City Studios . “He wears his heart on his sleeve,” said Macdonald. “He’s just so compelling to watch.” Macdonald, whose subjects have included Whitney Houston and Bob Marley, and who won an Oscar for One Day in September, believes his lack of interest in soccer was advantageous when following one of the greatest managers of all time. The docuseries charts Guardiola’s tumultuous final two seasons after winning an English record four Premier League titles in a row and follows in a long line of Amazon sports docs about soccer teams, although this one isn’t part of the streamer’s successful All or Nothing strand. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Netflix Unveils Live Darts Event With Teenage Sensation Luke Littler News "Remarkable True Story" Of Family Behind World-Famous Panini Stickers Told In Beta-Backed Italian Series 'Album Of Dreams' Asking stupid questions Kevin MacDonald. Image: Deadline via Getty “There’s something quite good about asking stupid questions,” Macdonald told Deadline. “I told him I didn’t know much about football and the weird thing was that really engaged him. He was like, ‘Oh my god I’m so fed up with talking about football.’ So we talked about books, films and all sorts of other things.” Macdonald’s disinterest in the UK’s national sport echoes that of Fisher Stevens, who directed Netflix’s smash hit Beckham documentary several years back and has also said in the past he didn’t know much about soccer when he took up the gig. It allowed Macdonald to get under Guardiola’s skin, the Scottish director explained. “I asked why he was so interested and why the players cared so much,” added Macdonald, who spent hours observing with the legendary Spanish coach, met him five times and interviewed him three times. “We tried to make a series that was emotional and human, and saw these players go through really dramatic events. I hope the series will be enjoyed by people who aren’t football fans, but are just interested in the human drama.” That drama came during the first few months of the period being covered in the doc as Guardiola, fresh off the back of his GOAT-like title quadruple, suddenly found results turning for the worst. Gavin Johnson, Group Media Director at City Football Group, who oversees City Studios, said filming this period was “quite uncomfortable for people internally,” but the team was commited to keeping the cameras rolling. “There is an acceptance at the top of the business that you have to tell deeper stories around the club and to do that you have to open yourself up,” said Johnson. “We’d had this amazing run and then we couldn’t stop losing for a short number of games and it was really really hard. Sometimes it was uncomfortable to watch but that is what makes good drama.” Macdonald said this created “authenticity and honesty,” which contrasts with the “first wave” of popular streaming sports docs from a few years back that “were quite constructed and quite limited” in scope. “Fans see that every Saturday,” he added. “They want something more – a kind of observational, vérité documentary that is quite rare in other worlds.” City Studios’ deep access comes from its unique position as an in-house Manchester City studio, chronicling the team all-year round. “The team we’ve built at City haven’t shied away from any area but have done a wonderful job to build trust, catch all of the content and work within the parameters we have to work within,” said Johnson. “These are top sports individuals [we are following] who have to try and win games for Man City. But also they’re human beings and that is the essence of what Kevin Macdonald has scratched below the surface of.” City Studios has a development deal with Sony Pictures Television for soccer content and Sony international boss Wayne Garvie has previously said he wants to find soccer’s Succession. Updating on the pact, Johnson said there are “three or four projects we are really excited about,” which lean on Garvie’s “expertise, contacts passion and knowledge,” but the world of scripted programming can be “frustratingly slow” compared with docs, he added. “The philosophical underpinning of the series” Image: City Studios So what next for Guardiola? Having won numerous titles at Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City, the 55-year-old is heading for a rare career break after turning down a job to manage the Italian national team. Macdonald said Guardiola is remarkably philosophical about the future. “He’s coming to terms with the idea that you cannot be the best forever, but you need to understand and communicate to those around you that you have to enjoy life whether you are winning or losing,” added Macdonald. “In a way that is the philosophical underpinning of the series. This feels very authentic coming from Pep. I kept telling him he was a natural Buddhist.” The docuseries launches August 19. It is directed by Macdonald alongside City Studios’ John De Caux and produced by Macdonald for Plan B/KM Films and Banijay UK-owned Workerbee, along with Johnson and Ged Doherty for City Studios. ‘Nashville’ & ‘Heroes’ Star Dies At 36; Career In Photos; Tributes Spidey Posts 2nd-Best Third Frame Ever; ‘Oak Street’ Out-Dinos ‘PAW Patrol’ Demands Huge Bond From AGs & WGA Over Costs Of “Roadblock” Suit HBO Renews ‘IT: Welcome To Derry’ For Season 2; Brad Caleb Kane Sole Showrunner Read More About: Comments

title: Everything We Know About ‘The Gilded Age’ Season 4 So Far
full_text: Skip to main content By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi Everything We Know About ‘The Morning Show’ Season 5 So Far Everything We Know About ‘The Gilded Age’ Season 4 So Far Everything We Know About ‘Percy Jackson And The Olympians’ Season 3 So Far View All August 17, 2026 3:19pm L-R: Carrie Coon and Merritt Wever in 'The Gilded Age' Season 3 HBO Max The culture clash will continue in Season 4 of Julian Fellowes’ HBO period drama The Gilded Age , based on the turn-of-the-century time period in America that lasted between 1870 and 1900 . Some familiar faces have been promoted to series regulars since Season 3, and some new faces are joining the cast to play big-name historical characters, among other new roles for the large ensemble. Related Stories News ‘The Gilded Age’ Cast Throughout The Seasons Of The Period Drama Cancellations and Renewals ‘The Gilded Age’ Renewed For Season 4 By HBO For everything we know about The Gilded Age Season 4, read on: When will The Gilded Age Season 4 come out? Watch on Deadline In a video promotion released in December, HBO hinted that the newest season of the period drama would arrive in 2026 . Is The Gilded Age Season 4 in production? The show’s fourth season has wrapped production. Star Carrie Coon posted the news on her Instagram story. How many episodes of T he Gilded Age Season 4 will there be in total? The Gilded Age ‘s fourth season will have a total of 8 episodes. Will there be new characters in The Gilded Age Season 4? Yes. Deadline broke the news in February that Taylor Trensch ( Bat Boy: The Musical ), James Scully ( You) , Dennis Haysbert ( 24 ), Maggie Kuntz ( John Proctor is the Villain ), Neal Huff ( Mare of Easttown ), and Tony Award-winner Bonnie Milligan ( Search Party ) would be joining the Season 4 cast in recurring roles. Jim Gaffigan ( Chappaquiddick ), Dallas Roberts ( Walk the Line ), Elizabeth Marvel ( Presumed Innocent ), and Andrew Burnap ( Snow White ) have joined as guest stars . Gaffigan will play Grover Cleveland, the 22nd President of the United States, who comes to New York to curry favor with the elite class. Roberts will portray Daniel Manning, a seasoned politician and Secretary of the Treasury under President Grover Cleveland. Marvel will play Nurse Virginia Saville, a kind nurse who works at the Neighborhood Settlement House in the Lower East Side. Burnap will portray Porter, a young gentleman of Society with an Ivy League education and money to invest in exciting new ventures. Who else is coming back to The Gilded Age Season 4? Jordan Donica, who plays Dr. William Kirkland, and Ashlie Atkinson, who portrays Mamie Fish, have been upped to series regulars for the upcoming fourth season. Kelley Curran, who plays Enid Winterton — formerly known as Turner when she served as Bertha’s (Carrie Coon) maid, has also been promoted to series regular . Denée Benton as Peggy Scott and Jordan Donica as Dr. Kirkland in ‘The Gilded Age’ Season 3 HBO Max Series regulars since Season 1 include Carrie Coon, Morgan Spector, Louisa Jacobson, Denee Benton, Cynthia Nixon, Christine Baranski, Harry Richardson, Blake Ritson, Taissa Farmiga, and Audra McDonald, who are all set to return. What happened in Season 3 of The Gilded Age ? Donica’s character, Dr. Kirkland, proposed to Peggy Scott (Benton) in a happy, joyful moment at the end of Season 3. In contrast, George (Spector) and Bertha hit some rough waters in their marriage. This was largely due to Bertha’s rolling full steam ahead by forcing their daughter Gladys (Farmiga) into an arranged marriage . George felt he had no control and was angered by Bertha not wanting her daughter to have a shot at a love match. It’s worth noting that George is upset on Gladys’s behalf; however, she married the Duke of Buckingham and ended up falling in love with him! Bertha’s sister Monica (Merritt Wever) came to town for the wedding, much to the former’s chagrin.

title: ‘All Her Fault’ Creator On Challenging How Society Views Women & Mothers In Thriller Series
full_text: Skip to main content By Katie Campione Katie Campione Senior TV & Labor Reporter @katie_campione More Stories By Katherine ‘Industry’ Adds Cary Elwes, Dianna Agron, Sam Riley & More As Season 5 Guests ‘All American’: Tensions High Within The Vortex Amid ICE Raid Aftermath & Fight For Beverly Coach In New Season 8 Clip ‘Lanterns’ Star Kyle Chandler Weighs In On Premiere Twist That Sets In Motion “The Whole Mystery” Of HBO Series View All August 17, 2026 3:15pm 'All Her Fault' showrunner Megan Gallagher at The London in West Hollywood on Sunday Griffin Nagel/Peacock Of all the feedback she’s received on All Her Fault , there is one comment that sticks with creator and showrunner Megan Gallagher : “Those are two of the worst husbands I’ve ever seen on television, and neither one of them were having an affair.” It certainly would’ve been easy (and predictable) to fuel audiences’ distaste for the spouses of Marissa Irvine (Sarah Snook) and Jenny Kaminski (Dakota Fanning), the two women at the center of the thriller who are brought together by the disappearance of the former’s son, by adding an extramarital relationship to the mix — particularly for Jenny’s husband, Richie (Thomas Cocquerel), whose sins amount to far less than Peter’s (Jake Lacy). Related Stories News ‘All Her Fault’ EPs On Creating Riveting Whodunnit Series With An Ending “You Don’t See Coming” – Crew Call Live News Emmy Nominations 2026: The Complete List But, it also would’ve undercut the themes Gallagher wanted to drive home with the limited series, which explores the ways that women and mothers often shoulder the brunt of societal responsibility and therefore get the lion’s share of the blame as well. Watch on Deadline “I don’t think that that’s the worst thing that you can do to your spouse, necessarily. I really don’t,” Gallagher said during an All Her Fault x Women in Entertainment FYC screening at The London in West Hollywood on Sunday. “The truth is, if you are Jenny Kaminsky, and you are miserable every day and asking for help every day, and the person who’s supposed to love you and be your life partner is doing everything within their power to keep you miserable, that’s so much worse, I think, than having an affair. Like, I’d rather have you sleep with your secretary than do that. It meant something to be able to get that on the screen, that look at marriage.” It also gave Gallagher an opportunity to dig into the complexities of a woman like Jenny, someone she says “might seem like [a] pushover” but is far from it. “She’s a people pleaser by nature. She’s very clearly depicted that way, as somebody whose strength is in being empathic and being intuitive and kind of sensing what other people need,” she explained. “And I feel like I know so many people like that, men and women both, but I think that those people often have a very steely core down there.” Gallagher describes the scene where Jenny finally puts her foot down with Richie as the character finally “finding that moment of no.” L-R: Megan Gallagher and Deadline’s Katie Campione onstage Griffin Nagel/Peacock Jenny’s realization is fueled not only by her husband’s actions throughout the series but also by the revelations about Marissa’s missing son and the part her own husband Peter played in his disappearance. At every turn, Marissa blames herself for Milo’s disappearance, as do others, and Peter lets her bear that undue weight for most of the series without explaining his part in any of it. Ultimately, Marissa is a devoted mom who had nothing to do with her son’s disappearance and who was fooled by her own husband. Just like with Jenny, Gallagher says she wanted to challenge expectations for the kind of woman Marissa would be. “I purposefully wrote Marissa as an incredibly accomplished career woman who wasn’t necessarily a lovey-dovey mom,” she said. “She’s got a real edge to her, in a good way, in a way that I find relatable. I’m not a wilting flower. She’s a really strong lady.” Marissa’s devotion to both her son and her own sense of self was an important component to get on screen, Gallagher said, adding: “It’s one thing when society blames you or the media blames you and all that kind of stuff. It’s another thing when women internalize this guilt and we take it on ourselves. To me, that’s the most heartbreaking part.” ‘Nashville’ & ‘Heroes’ Star Dies At 36; Career In Photos; Tributes Spidey Posts 2nd-Best Third Frame Ever; ‘Oak Street’ Out-Dinos ‘PAW Patrol’ Demands Huge Bond From AGs & WGA Over Costs Of “Roadblock” Suit HBO Renews ‘IT: Welcome To Derry’ For Season 2; Brad Caleb Kane Sole Showrunner Read More About: Comments

title: Dan Harmon Talks Overhauling ‘Rick And Morty’ Workplace, Fears & Hopes For Future Of Adult Animation – Contenders TV Nominees Studio
full_text: There was “a great deal of turbulence,” Dan Harmon acknowledged, following co-creator and star Justin Roiland’s 2023 ouster from Adult Swim ‘s Rick and Morty ahead of Season 7, amid domestic violence charges (which were ultimately dropped) and other allegations of misconduct. But it feels now, that the ship has been righted and the page has been turned. “This was a show that was grandfathered in from an era of less accountability, less awareness, less complication, and just creating a workplace where everybody felt human and grown up, that was enough to take several years,” said Rick and Morty co-creator, writer and executive producer Harmon at Deadline’s Contenders Television: The Nominees Studio, appearing alongside showrunner/EP Scott Marder . Related Stories News Vince Gilligan On The Mysteries Of 'Pluribus': "I Want People Who Watched The Show To Tell Me What It Means" - Contenders TV Nominees Studio News 'Love Story' Stars On Playing An Iconic Romance: The Fights, The Fashion And The New York Of The '90s - Contenders TV Nominees Studio Watch the conversation below and scroll down for photos from the event. One of the biggest behind-the-scenes shifts, Harmon said, has been fostering a workplace “where collaboration replaced the auteur model — where even an egomaniac like me could admit and benefit from the fact that people that went to art school actually know better than me how to tell a story.” Credited by Harmon as instrumental to the changes he described, Marder told us another facet of Rick and Morty ’s evolution has been creating a work environment that’s a bit less brutal — where systems were put in place to ensure the show wouldn’t “kill any one particular person” with work demands. “It’s a really tough show. We rewrite constantly, all that sort of stuff,” Marder noted. “By the time [Season] 9 was in place, all these systems were working and gelling, and morale was high.” Gratifying, for Marder, is the quality of work that has resulted from Rick and Morty ’s behind-the-scenes reboot. This year, Rick and Morty — a comedy chronicling the dimension-hopping misadventures of a cynical genius scientist and his anxious teenage grandson — scored its fifth Emmy nomination for Outstanding Animated Program. The show’s first nom since 2023 affords it a chance to win the category for a third time. “What’s cool about Season 9 is it’s the first one that I’ve heard people even put up there with the first two, which really feels rewarding,” said Marder. “I feel like Season 9 is the most in-sync flow we’ve had with the directors and art teams…which is why…people love the writing, but they also feel like the art has picked up, as well.” 01 L-R: Dan Harmon and Scott Marder Anthony Avellano for Deadline Dan Harmon Anthony Avellano for Deadline Scott Marder Anthony Avellano for Deadline L-R: Dan Harmon and Scott Marder Anthony Avellano for Deadline Scott Marder Anthony Avellano for Deadline During their chat with Deadline, the Rick and Morty duo confirmed that Season 10 is on track to premiere next summer. Joking that “it’s being generated by Palantir as we speak,” Harmon also spoke to his “cynical fear” for the future of adult animation — the question being, “how possible is this tomorrow?” Harmon argued that the Covid pandemic created “an illusion of huge demand” for this kind of content, but notes that animation has always been “a high-risk, high-yield thing.” “It’s not slop; it’s not driven by an algorithm,” Harmon said. “It takes longer to make your pilot than the average executive’s job is going to be secure. I don’t mean that to be crass because I could say the same thing about actors, writers, everybody. I mean, Venice is sinking.” The counterargument to Harmon’s cynicism is a show like Adult Swim’s Common Side Effects , which he described as being imbued with “a sort of unprecedented humanity.” “Fingers crossed, adult animation continues to be a thing. Because I believe that what Mike White does with White Lotus can be done even more effectively with animation,” Harmon said. “It’s a medium that that has a huge use for redeeming humanity.” Read More About: 5 Comments

Hargitay, best known for her long-running role of Captain Olivia Benson on NBC’s Law & Order: SVU, will star as the unnamed narrator who recounts a life marked by depression and domestic challenges and who has compiled a lifelong list of “every brilliant thing” that makes life worth living. At first the list is meant as a gift for the narrator’s troubled mother but eventually becomes a lifeline for the narrator as well. Written by Duncan Macmillan with Jonny Donahoe, and directed by Jeremy Herrin, Every Brilliant Thing is structed as a solo performance but with a twist: The sole scripted character – the narrator – interacts with audience members who stand in for various other characters. The play has been performed in over 80 countries including a hit production in London’s West End in 2025, which transferred to the Hudson Theatre on Broadway in February. Police dispatch audio obtained by TMZ reveals a friend of Panettiere’s called 911 at around 1:50 p.m. on Sunday reporting an “unresponsive female.” On the audio, medics were heard discussing an “overdose” and “cardiac arrest” around the time of her death. Paramedics attempted to resuscitate Panettiere using “advanced cardiac life support,” but she was pronounced deceased at the scene.

title: heartfelt tribute to Hayden Panettiere
full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Charles Esten Recounts Sweet First Encounter With Hayden Panettiere During ‘Nashville’ Audition: “What A Great Gift It Was To Act With You” “Just Heartbreak”: Connie Britton Mourns ‘Nashville’ Co-Star Hayden Panettiere ‘Clueless’ Eyes More OG Cast Returns Alongside Alicia Silverstone For Paramount+ Limited Series View All August 17, 2026 1:17pm (L-R): Connie Britton and Hayden Panettiere in 'Nashville' Disney General Entertainment Content Following her breakout role as cheerleader Claire Bennett on NBC’s Heroes , Hayden Panettiere in 2012 was cast as the co-lead opposite Connie Britton in the ABC country music drama Nashville . Following Panettiere’s passing at the age of 36 , Britton posted a heartfelt tribute on Instagram. Related Stories Obituaries Hayden Panettiere: Her Life & Career In Photos News Hayden Panettiere: Emma Roberts, Melissa Barrera, David Arquette, Viola Davis & More Pay Tribute To “Amazing Talent” “This was Hayden. Bursting with brilliance, shining so bright,” Britton wrote next to carousel of photos from Nashville . “I have no words for this sad song. Just heartbreak. I love you girl. Sleep easy now. 💔” Panettiere was actually the first of the two leads to be cast in the show, joined later by the Friday Night Lights star. The series centered on 40-year-old Nashville superstar Rayna James (Britton) who is stunned to find that her star is fading and her label requires her to team up with teen sensation Juliette Barnes (Panettiere) on tour–or else face the loss of her own tour and the label’s promotion of her latest record, whose sales have been underwhelming. It was the dynamic between Rayna and Juliette and the chemistry Britton and Panettiere that made Nashville a hit.
